newsitem.title: SPAIN: Tabacalera ups prices, helping margins.
newsitem.headline: Tabacalera ups prices, helping margins.

text.p: Spanish tobacco group Tabacalera S.A. raised its Virginia tobacco prices on Saturday in a long-delayed reaction to a summer tax hike, but analysts said the move would only partly alleviate tight margins.
Tabacalera raised prices on all its Virginia, or blond, tobacco including leading brands Fortuna and Nobel, by 20 pesetas per pack to 220.

In August, Tabacalera raised prices in response to the tax hike on its black, largely domestic tobacco brands, but had declined to pass on the hike in the more internationally competitive blond sector in order to maintain market share.

In a brief statement, the firm said it "preferred the correct positioning of its brands in market volume in the medium- to long-term (despite) a short-term loss of margin. Having achieved this objective, Tabacalera has decided to raise prices."
On Monday, international competitors R.J.Reynolds, Philip Morris and BAT followed suit.
Analysts said the move was positive for the stock, despite the fact that the firm was still far from recovering the profit margin it had before the tax hike.
Tabacalera rose 50 pesetas, or nearly one percent, to 5,130 on Monday, while the Ibex-35 index added 0.38 percent to 4,685.33.

"This (the hike in prices) is good for the stock. For (Tabacalera's) accounts it seems good as they correct half of the effect they were suffering in the past few months," said an analyst at Credit Lyonnais Securities (CLS) in Madrid.
"But they haven't fully passed on the tax hike. In terms of margins they had lost around 10 pesetas by maintaining prices, and they recover around five with this rise," he said.

An analyst at Sociedad de Bolsa said that in order to recoup the tax hike and maintain the previous profit margin, the price of Nobel or Fortuna should have to have been raised to 238 pesetas instead of 220 pesetas.
Most analysts believe market shares will be maintained, despite the fact that Tabacalera's price hike was bigger than those applied to competitors Winston, Marlboro and Camel.

"More expensive brands such as Winston or Malboro are even more price sensitive, and maybe for that reason they moderated the increase so...that people don't switch to cheaper brands," said another analyst.
But analysts worried that even the modest price increases could risk sales.

"We'll have to see how the rise affects sales volume. We're in a clear consumer slump and I think firms intend to sacrifice part of their earnings to maintain market share, but we'll have to see how consumers behave in the near-term," said the Sociedad de Bolsa analyst.

For the first nine months of the year, Tabacalera posted a 4.7 percent rise in pre-tax profit. But sales net of taxes and commissions, hit by a governmnet tax increase on tobacco in July, fell 6.3 percent to 238.58 billion pesetas.
